# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👈 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👉 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]

I see display 0, orange light, and three wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute’s gesture appears to encode an instruction, but I do not yet know its code; I will provide the full visible state to both listeners.

``` 
speak(text="Bomb view: display reads 0. Light is orange. Wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊]

The display and wires are unchanged, but the light has changed from orange to green. Mute’s two-symbol gesture is not yet interpretable to me, so I should continue giving the observable state verbally to support Blind’s action and Mute’s manual guidance.

```text
speak(text="Update: the light is now green. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

The light is now red. I still cannot safely interpret Mute’s gestures: the earlier long sequence, then two fists, then an open hand do not have an agreed meaning. I will report the change and establish a simple gesture-to-action protocol with Mute, so that I can relay a definite instruction to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0; light is now red; wires are still 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. No action instruction confirmed yet.")

speak(to="mute", text="I cannot decode your gestures. Please use this protocol for the required action: gesture 👍 means tell Blind cut wire 1; 👎 means cut wire 2; 👌 means cut wire 3; ✊ means wait/no cut. Send exactly one of those.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

Mute used the agreed symbol ✊, meaning wait/no cut. The light has returned to orange; display remains 0 and wire order is unchanged. I will tell Blind not to cut anything.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Do not cut any wire: Mute's instruction is WAIT. Current view: display 0, orange light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]

Mute again signals ✊ under the agreed protocol, so the instruction remains to wait and not cut. The light is green; display and wires are unchanged.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute again says WAIT: do not cut. Current view: green light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new manual instruction arrived from Mute this turn. The light is red again, while the display remains 0 and wire order remains red, yellow, blue. With no confirmed change from the manual, Blind should continue to wait.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current bomb view: red light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please send the agreed single gesture if an action is required.")

speak(to="blind", text="No new instruction from Mute. Continue waiting; do not cut. Current view: red light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

Mute sends ✊ again, which in the agreed protocol means wait/no cut. The light is orange, with display 0 and unchanged wires.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute says WAIT again. Do not cut any wire. Current view: orange light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]

Mute again uses ✊, the established wait/no-cut signal. The green light is likely part of a repeating cycle; display and wire arrangement remain unchanged. Blind should not act without a distinct instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute again signals WAIT. Do not cut or operate anything. View: green light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

(empty)

The light is red again, completing the observed orange–green–red cycle, and there is no new instruction from Mute. The display remains 0 and the wires are unchanged. I will tell Blind to continue waiting and remind Mute of the present state.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="No new manual instruction; continue waiting and do not cut. Current view: red light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")

speak(to="mute", text="Current state is red light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Send the agreed action gesture if the manual calls for one.")
```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]

Mute again sends the agreed ✊ signal, meaning wait/no cut. The bomb remains at display 0 with the same three wires, and the light is orange. Blind should continue not to operate it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signals WAIT again. Do not cut or operate anything. Current view: orange light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 11

LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

There is no new instruction from Mute. The light is green, display remains 0, and the wire order is unchanged. I will continue the safe wait instruction and ask Blind to report any tactile controls or changes, since Blind’s earlier gestures may have been an attempted report.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="No new instruction from Mute; keep waiting. View: green light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please describe aloud any controls, labels, or changes you can feel.")

speak(to="mute", text="View update: green light; display 0; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. If the manual requires action at a particular light or display condition, send the agreed action gesture then.")
```
